record.tranche_reason: The paper compares convolutional, locally connected and fully connected image classifiers and reports how local connectivity relates to test accuracy. It also tests whether a sparsity training method can help fully connected networks learn local connections.
record.gate_note: The paper tests V3. Other claim versions are not tested: the width plots do not test the stated one-hidden-layer ReLU setup or an interpolation-threshold peak; the paper does not test random-label memorization, optimizer comparisons, large-batch penalties, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples. Table 2 includes prior-work comparisons; rows below cover the paper's own s-fc results. Figure-only trends are not reconstructed as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: This is an original source for V3. Its own image-classification experiments compare convolutional, locally connected and fully connected networks using test accuracy, and test whether learning sparse local connections narrows the architecture gap. No verdict labels are issued because the study is an original source for V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify local connectivity as the main contributor to the architecture advantage in their comparisons and report that β-lasso learns sparse local filters while substantially narrowing the accuracy gap. These observations do not isolate locality as the cause of β-lasso's improvement.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares architecture families and introduces β-lasso, an L1-based sparsity training method with thresholding; its experiments use image classification, batch size 512, cosine annealing and data augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture depth, local connectivity, weight sharing, training duration (400 versus 4000 epochs), and β-lasso threshold setting affect reported performance. The authors report that longer training narrows the shallow/deep gap, while the benefit of depth disappears without weight sharing.

fits_no_version.finding: β-lasso improves ResNet18 test accuracy over SGD across the tested kernel sizes on all three datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparsity-promoting training can improve convolutional classifiers, particularly with larger kernels.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The comparisons use selected hyperparameters: the appendix says models with the highest validation accuracy among tried choices were picked. The paper reports β-lasso comparisons against convolutional/local architectures but does not isolate whether the accuracy gap closes because of learned local connectivity alone.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's 400-epoch results for d-conv, d-local, d-fc, s-conv, s-local and s-fc on CIFAR10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN are omitted; the 4000-epoch comparisons are retained for each. Table 1 also reports 3-fc and its 400/4000-epoch results; omitted as an additional fully connected architecture comparison. Table 2's cited prior-work values are not included because they are results attributed to other studies.

untested.parts: Joint natural-label and fixed-random-label training and held-out performance.
Whether test error continues falling beyond the width required for zero training error. The architecture scaling plots do not establish this threshold comparison.
MNIST; fully connected networks initialized from trained convolutional networks. The experiments also do not isolate learned locality as the causal mediator of β-lasso's accuracy improvement.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epochs and adaptations that remove their penalty.
An isolated dropout comparison. Dropout is a hyperparameter choice, but its separate results are not reported.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Architecture scaling comparisons show s-conv outperforming 3-fc across model sizes, with d-conv and ResNet18 performing better still. These provide V3 evidence beyond the single architecture sizes in Table 1; exact curve values are not readable from the supplied text.

The evidence for learned locality is missing: β-lasso produces sparse local first-layer filters, whereas SGD produces dense, locally correlated filters; the first-layer nonzero count falls below s-local's parameter count. Accuracy rows alone do not record this component of V3.

record.verdict_notes: All 27 accuracy values match the supplied tables. Comparisons use validation-selected hyperparameters, data augmentation and batch normalization; SGD tuning includes momentum, weight decay and dropout. No uncertainty estimates are supplied. V3 verdict labels are suppressed because arXiv:2007.13657 is an explicitly listed original source.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
MNIST; the cited d’Ascoli et al. initialization result; explicit comparisons on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN are reported here.
Large versus small batch comparisons and adaptations to batch size.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

relation.reason: Its own image-classification experiments compare convolutional, locally connected and fully connected architectures and measure gap narrowing under β-lasso.

tranche.reason: This is an original source for V3; its architecture comparisons and β-lasso experiments supply the original method and test-accuracy measurements.

source_check.notes: The existing observed states fit V3's gap-narrowing clause; equality with convolution is not required. β-specific locality visualizations are not separately supplied for β=0 or β=1, and the study does not isolate locality as the cause of improvement or report uncertainty for these table values.
